AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Rebollo called meeting to order at 5:07 p.m. 

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on the Closed Session agenda.  

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION The City Council/Successor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:08 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/Successor Agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:11 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session items: 

Item #1.C. was discussed before the regular City Council meeting. The staff made a presentation, the City Council provided feedback, and no reportable action was taken on this item. 

City Attorney Tapia stated that formatting errors were fixed on the proposed City Manager's agreement, and copies are available for public viewing. 

City Attorney Tapia reported at 10:04 p.m. on item #1.A and 1.B - The staff made a presentation, the City Council provided feedback, and no reportable action was taken on these items. 

Items #2 and #3 were not discussed in the Closed Session. 


6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Rebollo called meeting to order at 6:11 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Human Resources Director Pappo led the Pledge of Allegiance

INVOCATION Councilmember Garcia offered the invocation. 

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

3.. Proclaiming March 21, 2023, as World Down Syndrome Day Director of Parks and Recreation Alaniz provided a presentation regarding World Down Syndrome Day. Susana Cisneros, Commission on Disabilities Access and Opportunities, spoke about the importance of advocacy and teaching everyone how to be a change-maker and respect. 

Mayor Rebollo asked residents to post photos on the Parks and Recreation page on Instagram and Facebook; she would do a raffle for two $100 gift cards. In addition, Mayor Rebollo encouraged residents to watch the movie "Champions" and stated that she would add raffle tickets for two families to see "Champions."


1.. Recognition to the Unplugged Cast & Crew Mayor Rebollo and Councilmembers recognized Unplugged cast and crew for their performance of Willy Wonka.  

8.. Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department Regarding Public Safety in the City of Commerce Sergeant Duarte provided a Powerpoint presentation with the last two weeks of statistics and updates. There has been a homeless clean-up, and Deputies participated in the Read Across America. Councilmembers and Mayor thanked Sergeant Duarte for the presentation and homeless clean-up. 

Vice Mayor Argumedo pointed out a decrease in crime and asked what it is attributed to. Sergeant Duarte responded that most burglaries occur in Commerce Center and Citadel Outlets. While Citadel Outlets has two deputies assigned, most burglaries happen when Deputies are not on the shift. Sergeant Duarte also added that she is meeting with Target's management to see how they could prevent crime better or make arrests more prompt and deter crime in that area.   


PUBLIC COMMENT Lisa Cortez, and Natalia Vaneros talked about crush volleyball and asked for support for the teams to go to National Volleyball Tournament in Florida.  

Ricky Alavera also spoke about amazing girls in those teams and asked for the Council's support. 




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez

6.. Approval of Minutes

5.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 14A,  and 14B

12.. Second Reading and Adoption of an Ordinance Approving a Zoning Ordinance Text Amendment: To Amend Section 19.21.130 (Loading and Unloading Requirements) of the City of Commerce Municipal Code To Limit the Hours of Loading and Unloading in Manufacturing Zoned Properties when Located Within 300 Feet of Properties Located in the City’s R-1 and R-2 Zones  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Mayor Rebollo read public comment letters submitted by Jon Reno, Managing Director of Jones Lang LaSalle Brokerage, Inc, Robert Taylor, Executive Director of Commerce Industrial Council, and Timothy Jemal, CEO of NAIOP SoCal, opposing the passage of the proposed ordinance. 

Acting Director of Economic Development and Planning Esparza provided a brief overview of the staff report. 

Councilmember Garcia recommended continuing this item. 

City Manager Cisneros stated that this item was presented to the Planning Commission in 2021 and 2022 but has not been acted upon. There was a hearing on January 26, 2023, by the Planning Commission, and on February 28, 2023, the ordinance was introduced, and no comments were received at that time. City Manager Cisneros recommended that existing operators apply for a Conditional Use Permit at no cost and go through the hearing at the Planning Commission. The new businesses would have to pay for a Conditional Use Permit. According to City Manager Cisneros, this would create a balance between the residents and the business community, and he recommended moving forward with the second reading of the ordinance. 




SCHEDULED MATTERS

11.. Committee and Commission Appointments Vice Mayor Argumedo appointed Ester Zavala to Planning Commission and Alex Rendon to Measure AA Advisory Committee. 

ORDINANCES

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Lainez congratulated Ester Zavala on her appointment to the Planning Commission. 

Councilmembers and the Mayor recognized Parks and Recreation and other departments involved in putting a great Employee Recognition event.

Mayor Rebollo congratulated Johncito Pereza for being appointed Congressional representative for Congressman Garcia. Mayor Rebollo invited everyone to Mayor's Prayer Breakfast on Saturday.

City Council recessed to a Closed Session at 8:28 p.m.


ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 10:06 p.m.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.


Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.

4.. Library Director Introduction Assistant City Manager Domic introduced Sonia Batista as the new Library Director.

2.. Camp Commerce Recognition/Report - Above and Beyond Director of Parks and Recreation Alaniz provided a presentation regarding hush conditions at Camp Commerce and how staff managed to resolve snow removal and maintaining the facility. 

9.. Parks & Recreation Recruitment Day Parks and Recreation Director Alaniz provided an overview of recruitment efforts. According to Director, 20 staff members put this recruitment day event together. Council Members thanked Director Alaniz and staff for their efforts and congratulated him on the successful event. 


10.. Mid-Year Budget Review  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Assistant City Manager Domic provided an overview and stated that the projected surplus is estimated at 4.5 million for 2022/2023 end of the fiscal year.

Discussion took place about hiring a Public Safety Manager or Director and whether it could be included in the budget now. According to Assistant City Manager Domic, the City Council could allocate $43,600 for this fiscal year's Public Safety Manager position to manage public safety contracts better and oversee the CSO program.

Councilmember Lainez asked whether the automated license plate reader program could be included in this year's budget by allocating funds for this program. According to Assistant City Manager Domic, staff will present various public safety recommendations at the upcoming Council meeting, and an automated license plate reader is one of those. In response to Mayor Rebollo, whether previously allocated funds for the automated license reader program are still available, Assistant City Manager Domic stated that those were eliminated.

Councilmember Garcia asked about the increase in recruitment costs and what requested funds are needed for staffing or supplies. City Manager Cisneros stated that with the recent increase in hiring, supplies and some staffing cost needs to be covered, especially for the latest hiring event for Parks and Recreation, which took place on the weekend.

Councilmember Garcia inquired about several Parks and Recreation requested items, whether for this fiscal year or next, and construction starting in the Veteran's park shortly and whether funds need to be allocated for that area. The Director of Parks and Recreation, Alaniz, stated that most of the supplies were reduced during the pandemic, and those funds are needed to bring back most of the programming and additional staffing. City Manager Cisneros responded that those requests are for staffing mainly for this year, purchasing supplies, and getting some of it before the fiscal year starts. 

According to City Manager Cisneros, construction might be postponed in Veteran's park; therefore, requested funds would ensure that programming is provided and staffing is available until the end of the fiscal year.

Councilmember Garcia asked for the breakdown of the Crush volleyball tournament request, how staffing/chaperons were selected to go with the team, and whether Arizona travel reimbursement is the reoccurring expense or the new one. City Manager Cisneros stated that Arizona reimbursement expense is the first-time expense, but this places other teams in parity with the aquatics teams.

In response to Councilmember Garcia's question regarding economic development funds required for Commerce Rail Analysis, City Manager Cisneros stated that economic development funds are the estimated amount and submissions from qualified companies would be solicited and brought back for the City Council approval. Transportation request regarding carpet replacement is a safety issue that must be addressed. 

Further discussion took place about the parity for all travel teams. Mayor Rebollo added that sometimes, certain travel could be predicted. Still, once the team qualifies for the tournament, that is hard to budget and recommended to have further discussion about this and maybe allocate a fund for those unforeseen travel for the travel teams.

It was a consensus between the City Council to add Public Safety Manager to the budget.




7.. Consideration of Employment Agreement with City Manager
